item.title: Kolhapur man ‘pushes’ girlfriend into 1,000ft valley after family fixes her marriage
item.description: Tarrannum Naik, a 23-year-old engineering student, was found dead in a valley near Naikwadi waterfall. Her boyfriend, Sripad Vadar, was arrested after police discovered inconsistencies in his statements. He initially claimed Tarrannum fell into the valley, but chat history indicated he was upset about her arranged marriage. The police are awaiting a postmortem report to determine the cause of her death.

item.title: SBI warns of 'Jumped Deposit Scam': What it is and how to stay safe
item.description: The State Bank of India has alerted its customers about a rising threat known as the Jumped Deposit Scam, targeting online banking users. In this deceptive scheme, fraudsters make small deposits to build trust before compelling victims to approve larger payments. The bank recommends customers to be vigilant against suspicious communications, immediately block any questionable contacts, and report any unexpected transactions to prevent falling victim to this manipulation.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: ‘Plan B’ against Abhishek Sharma revealed! India star says he knew WI's strategy
item.description: Abhishek Sharma's dynamic performance with a blistering 69 runs played a crucial role in propelling India to a total against the West Indies. With determined bowling efforts, India successfully limited the visitors to 209 runs, clinching the match by 14 runs. West Indies all-rounder Shamar Springer mentioned their strategy to curb Sharma's aggressive play. Despite facing tough opposition, India showcased resilience, taking a 2-1 lead in the five-match T20I series.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Taxman alleged IT park firm was a tax dodge; ITAT rules for five landowners
item.description: In 2005, the landowners and the same builder executed a registered joint development agreement (JDA). Under the arrangement, the builder was granted development rights and a Power of Attorney (POA) was executed for various purposes. The builder also paid the landowners a refundable, interest-free deposit of Rs 37.25 lakh.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Tyler Perry’s $750,000 gift helped pay back taxes for 300 Atlanta seniors
item.description: Tyler Perry has made a significant donation of $750,000 to assist low-income senior citizens in Atlanta. This contribution will help more than 300 seniors pay overdue property taxes and remain in their homes. Additionally, it will support a pilot program for another 100 seniors facing property tax increases. Mayor Dickens emphasized the importance of preserving the homes of longstanding residents amid Atlanta's growth.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Michigan couple loses court fight over 50-foot strip claimed through deed error
item.description: A Michigan couple has lost a legal battle over a 50-foot-wide strip of land they claimed was wrongly excluded from their property because of an error in a 1965 deed. The couple, who bought their land at a 2015 tax sale, argued that previous owners had used the disputed area for decades. However, two surveys placed the land within their neighbour's property. On October 9, 2026, the Michigan Court of Appeals ruled against the couple, citing insufficient evidence to establish ownership.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Couple rejects $131,000 offer for data center power line on their property
item.description: Jerry Zelenka has turned down an offer from American Transmission Company for a power line on his property. The proposal involves clearing trees and demolishing several buildings near his home, prompting Zelenka's concerns. He feels the compensation does not reflect the value of his property or the destruction planned. Zelenka fears the use of eminent domain if an agreement is not reached.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Meet Arya Satheesh, 18, who invented plant-based plastic to fight microplastics
item.description: At just 18, Arya Satheesh from Ireland has pioneered Eco Purge, a groundbreaking biodegradable plastic designed to combat plastic pollution effectively. This smart material not only decomposes but also emits enzymes that actively break down microplastics in the ecosystem. Inspired by her discovery of water contaminants, Satheesh aims to shed light on the crucial issue of plastic waste.
item.dc:creator: MANISHA GUPTA

item.title: Bizarre run-out! Tilak Varma’s casual approach leads to unusual dismissal
item.description: India batter Tilak Varma was involved in an unusual run-out during the third T20I against West Indies on Sunday after a misunderstanding with Axar Patel cost him his wicket. The incident took place in the 17th over, with Gudakesh Motie bowling to Axar. The Indian all-rounder flicked a low full toss towards deep backward square leg, where Kamil Pooran dived to prevent the ball from reaching the boundary.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: When Delhi cops played catch-up with protesters
item.description: In a fervent demonstration, protesters in Delhi sought to reach Jantar Mantar, advocating for the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner. AISA leader Neha Bora and several participants faced detention as police intervened, triggering a chaotic chase. Bora criticized the cramped conditions of the police bus, emphasizing the ongoing demands for accountability and democratic integrity from those in power.
item.dc:creator: MEGHNA DHULIA

item.title: Brisbane homeowner revives warranty claim after defects led to $500,000 estimate
item.description: A homeowner in Brisbane encountered severe hurdles when dealing with a building plagued by significant structural flaws. The Queensland Building and Construction Commission initially denied his claim, but a tribunal later overturned this ruling. With nine major defects needing repairs estimated at over $500,000, any compensation may still fall short due to statutory limits. The QBCC is now reviewing his claim for possible reimbursement.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Wonga Park home with 160-metre miniature railway sells for $1.375 million
item.description: Wonga Park in Australia has witnessed remarkable appreciation in property value, rising from A$420,000 in 2005 to A$1.375 million by 2025. This enchanting home boasts a 160-metre miniature railway, picturesque gardens, a chicken coop, and stunning vistas of the Dandenong Ranges. Its allure is further enhanced by five bedrooms and unique features, ensuring it remains a sought-after gem among buyers over the years.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Taylor Swift’s $4m Nashville education centre now showcases local student art
item.description: In 2012, Taylor Swift donated $4 million to create an education center at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. This center focuses on engaging children and families with the history of country music. Currently, it hosts an exhibition called Connection featuring works by students and artists from Friends Life Community. Participants learn letterpress printing techniques and create their own unique posters.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 'You don’t even let us go near the aircraft': As IAF trains with F-35s, US guards secrets
item.description: The US Air Force showcased the F-35 at Exercise Tarang Shakti while maintaining strict security controls. Air Chief Marshal AP Singh expressed frustration about limited access to the aircraft. He raised concerns about India's own fifth-generation fighter development, urging for expedited processes. India's current fighter strength faces challenges due to delays in deliveries of Tejas Mk-1A. The IAF is actively planning to acquire additional Rafale aircraft to enhance capabilities.
item.dc:creator: DHRUV YADAV

item.title: Delhi Metro shuts 6 stations till 4pm amid Congress march; traffic curbs likely
item.description: Entry and exit at six Delhi Metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat and Patel Chowk, will remain closed from 6 am to 4 pm on Monday due to security concerns amid Congress' call for a protest march to the Supreme Court, while interchange facilities will continue to be available at the affected stations, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: Can keeping your phone in your pocket harm sperm health?
item.description: Research shows that exposure to radiofrequency from mobile phones may negatively impact sperm motility and viability in men. Although studies have reported inconsistent connections between phone carrying and sperm count or fertility, oxidative stress remains a significant factor affecting sperm quality. Nutritional supplements like Coenzyme Q10, zinc, and vitamin C may help improve sperm health by combating oxidative damage.
item.dc:creator: TIMESOFINDIA.COM

item.title: 20 goals, 3 wins! India U17 women make history with Asian Cup qualification feat
item.description: India's U17 women's football team has etched its name in history once again by securing a spot in their second consecutive Women’s Asian Cup. They dominated in the AFC qualifiers, thrashing Malaysia 4-0. Key contributions came from Redima Devi Chingkhamayum, Pritika Barman, Anushka Kumari, and Nidhi, who collectively showcased the extraordinary talent emerging in women's football in India with 20 goals throughout the tournament.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: ‘Punched in eyes, pushed into bus’: Journalists detained for second day despite IDs
item.description: Journalists covering protests in New Delhi faced detainment by police during their reporting duties. Despite showing valid press credentials, several journalists were forcibly taken into police vans. Among those detained were individuals from established media organizations and independent outlets. The police reportedly acted aggressively towards journalists, leading to injuries and humiliations. This situation raises concerns about media freedom in the capital amidst ongoing protests.
item.dc:creator: MEGHNA DHULIA, KOUSHIKI SAHA, G S DHANUSH

item.title: Mumbai is already thirsty: Why the 2041 problem is really a 2026 problem
item.description: Mumbai is experiencing a significant water crisis due to a supply deficit of over 500 million liters daily. The city's demand for water is expected to soar by 57% by 2041, surpassing current supply capabilities. Various infrastructure projects intended to enhance water supply are either delayed or in early planning stages. Desalination plants are in development, but they will only partially address the water shortage.
item.dc:creator: BIJU MATHEW

item.title: ‘Dad will take care of it’: 3 killed as teen’s Mini Cooper rams scooter in Kochi
item.description: A speeding luxury hatchback driven by Suhail Sajeev crashed into a scooter, killing three youths instantly. Police arrested Suhail on charges of culpable homicide, with indications of him being intoxicated. Witnesses reported the car was speeding excessively on the airport road in Nedumbassery. An investigation is underway regarding the alcohol served to Suhail, who is underage, while his co-passenger was also arrested.

item.title: Buried under Greenland’s ice: The secret US Army base Nasa rediscovered in 2024
item.description: The hidden U.S. military base, Camp Century, built beneath Greenland's glaciers during the late 1950s, has resurfaced in a NASA radar scan revealing its intricate layout. Known for housing a nuclear reactor and various toxic materials, the site poses significant environmental risks as Greenland's ice diminishes. This finding compels us to confront the implications of historical military operations in light of our planet's shifting climate.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: After 15 years, Team India tailender achieves rare T20I feat
item.description: Prince Yadav has joined S Sreesanth and Ravichandran Ashwin on a rare list of Indian batters after hitting three fours against the West Indies in the third T20I in Indore on Sunday. He became only the third Indian batter batting at No. 10 or No. 11 to hit at least three boundaries in a T20 International.

item.title: Oregon blimp hangar sold for $1 after storm damage; air museum set to reopen
item.description: An 83-year-old World War II-era blimp hangar in Oregon, US, was sold for just $1 after a storm tore a 200-foot hole in its roof in December 2025. The historic building, which houses the Tillamook Air Museum, was purchased by a nonprofit organisation and is set to reopen on October 29 after nearly 10 months of closure.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Colorado woman protects 18,484 acres of family ranch once listed for $100 million
item.description: A Colorado woman has permanently protected 18,484 acres of her family's cattle ranch, once listed for $100 million, from future development. Susan Nottingham's decision preserves land her parents spent over 60 years assembling, along with historic water rights linked to the Colorado River. The agreement also protects wildlife habitats while allowing the ranch to continue agricultural operations.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Syria reopens 1,600-year-old Byzantine church complex after restoration
item.description: After extensive restoration, the Deir Samaan Citadel, a remarkable ancient religious complex in northern Syria, has reopened its doors to visitors. Established in the fifth century, this site holds immense significance for Christian pilgrims. Having endured damage from natural calamities, conflict, and neglect, recent efforts aimed to repair visitor pathways and rehabilitate essential facilities. This reopening forms part of a larger initiative to encourage tourism in the Aleppo province.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Man killed in fight over Delhi metro seat; retired IAS officer, son held
item.description: A 48-year-old man named Pawan Sharma died following an assault in a Delhi Metro train. The incident occurred due to a dispute over a senior citizen seat during his journey. His mother, Durga Devi, witnessed the altercation between her son and the accused men. Both the alleged assailants, a retired IAS officer and his son, have been arrested by Delhi Metro Police.
item.dc:creator: ABHAY

item.title: Delhi-NCR wakes up to heavy rain, thunderstorms as IMD issues red alert
item.description: Delhi experienced heavy rain and thunderstorms on Monday morning, leading to a noticeable change in weather. The India Meteorological Department predicted moderate to heavy rainfall for the next few hours. While cooler temperatures prevail, maximum temperatures are expected to range between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius. The IMD also forecasted partly cloudy skies and no rainfall over the next six days.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: World Cup setback fuelled the gold run in Asian Games: Shilanand Lakra
item.description: India's men's hockey team transformed their World Cup disappointment into a golden opportunity at the Asian Games. Learning from past mistakes was crucial, as underlined by Shilanand Lakra, who pointed out the vital role of teamwork and steady progress. Their intense 4-3 win against Pakistan was a highlight, and with Olympic qualification now in hand, the team is fueled with ambition for even greater achievements ahead.
item.dc:creator: ARNAB LALL SEAL

item.title: Florida family protects 498-acre cattle ranch in $7.48m conservation deal
item.description: A 498-acre cattle ranch known as Turnpike Dairy has been protected from future development through a conservation easement. The agreement allows the managing family to continue agricultural operations on the property. Martin County contributed $3.74 million towards the $7.48 million deal to preserve the land. This conservation effort is part of Florida’s Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, which protects working farms.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Washington farmer challenges $618,000 irrigation penalties in state Supreme Court
item.description: Ron Fodé, a dedicated farmer from Washington State, is fighting against hefty penalties threatening his agricultural livelihood due to irrigation practices. The conflict arose in 2017 over water rights for his crops, leading to the Department of Ecology rejecting his irrigation assistance applications. This has resulted in penalties totaling $618,000.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Why kids who shop with parents learn a hidden life skill
item.description: Grocery shopping transforms into a valuable lesson in financial literacy when parents involve their children in decision-making processes. By allowing kids to make age-appropriate choices, parents help them grasp essential mathematical skills through real-life applications. This collaborative shopping experience not only strengthens the parent-child bond but also equips children with critical money management skills for their future.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
